A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same activation-based FFN-to-MoE framework. All 14 pages of v2 and 13 pages of v3, including their figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison despite extensive revision and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original perplexity, downstream accuracy, inference timing and ablation results, including calibration and model-scaling experiments in Appendices B and C.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, calibration analyses, efficiency measurements and self-consistency experiments in Sections 5.2-5.4.

M1.justification: The core activation profiling, balanced clustering, representative-neuron router and fine-tuning rules remain. Section 4.4 adds recursive application inside existing MoE experts, creating primary and subexpert routing. v3 also evaluates optional self-consistency voting. These extend deployment procedures while retaining the underlying construction.

E1.justification: v3 adds ARC-Easy, MMLU, HumanEval and GSM8K, plus math/science and code activation profiling using Nemotron and OpenCoder data. BoolQ, SciQ and SlimPajama extended fine-tuning disappear. WikiText-2, C4, PIQA, WinoGrande, ARC-Challenge and HellaSwag remain.

E2.justification: Main comparisons add SliceGPT, SLEB and EMoE alongside retained LLaMA-MoE variants. v3 Table 5 evaluates MoEfication, G-MoEfication, READ-ME and router-replacement variants; Table 8 adds WINA. The Pythia-1.0B/TinyLlama-1.1B comparison is removed, and LLaMA-MoE no longer participates in the perplexity comparison.

E3.justification: v3 replaces Llama-3 8B and Llama-2 13B evaluations with Llama-2 70B and several Qwen models, and emphasizes S3A3E8 at 25% sparsity, equivalent to v2's 75% activation. WinoGrande, ARC-Challenge and HellaSwag change from 5/25/10-shot to reported zero-shot evaluation. New protocols include FLOPs/MACs/throughput measurements, 4k/32k contexts and k=1/5 voting. Several LLaMA-MoE baseline scores remain identical despite changed shot labels, so reruns are not established.

E4.justification: v3 adds cross-domain shared-neuron overlap, clustering/router replacement ablations, WINA composition, a finer sparsity sweep and self-consistency analysis. Calibration, fine-tuning-size and expert-configuration studies are revised, predominantly at 75% activation rather than v2's 25%. Extended SlimPajama and 13B calibration studies disappear. The activation histograms and load-balancing plot are retained evidence, not new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. v3's k=1/5 self-consistency experiment changes inference sampling and voting, rather than introducing uncertainty estimation for reported results.

E6.justification: Numerous results are added, replaced or removed. For Llama-2 7B at the corresponding 75% activation level, v2 Table 1 reports training-free/fine-tuned WikiText-2 PPL of 7.02/5.69, while v3 Table 3 reports 7.32/5.92. New results include 44.02% MMLU, 11.22% HumanEval and 13.01% GSM8K in v3 Table 2. Revised accuracy and speed measurements often use different settings and do not establish uniform same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Most clustering and router mathematics is retained, condensed and moved into Appendix A. v3 adds an expected squared reconstruction-error objective in Equation 2, the binary-feature squared-L2/Hamming identity in Appendix A.3, and an O(n^3) assignment-complexity statement. These are limited formal additions to the existing approximate argument.

C1.justification: v3 retains analytical construction with optional lightweight fine-tuning but expands the contribution to hierarchical sparsification of existing MoEs and compatibility with other efficiency techniques. The abstract and introduction replace v2's lossless-perplexity, 1.5x acceleration and greater-than-76% recovery claims with up to 1.17x compute-bound speedup and broader comparison claims under lightweight adaptation.

C2.justification: v3 interprets calibration stability and cross-domain neuron overlap as evidence of intrinsic activation structure, while retaining the domain-representativeness caveat. It adds explanations involving scattered frequently active neurons, implicit regularization, routing variance and self-consistency, plus extensive compatibility discussion. Limitations newly specify English benchmarks, decoder-only architectures and increased generation variance.

D1.justification: The calibration size, LoRA settings, optimizer, learning rates and code-access disclosure remain. v3 explicitly names the assignment solver, states that baselines were reimplemented, and reports 4.5-minute construction and 46-minute total processing times. However, v2 Appendix A's instruction to normalize inputs and projection weights is omitted; this establishes lost documentation, not a proven procedural change.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands to cover EMoE, G-MoEfication, READ-ME, ReMoE, Lory, SLEB, TEAL and WINA. v3 distinguishes its shared experts from MoEBERT's duplicated neurons and acknowledges MoEfication's co-activation clustering alternative. Several earlier compression references disappear. The changes materially refine novelty and complementarity positioning beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, methodology and discussion. A dedicated activation-pattern motivation section precedes the method, detailed mathematics moves into a reorganized Appendix A, and discussion and limitations become substantial main-text sections.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout with extensively restructured tables. v2 Figure A.1 becomes main-text Figures 1 and 2; the overview and load-balancing graphics are retained and relocated. The data-efficiency plot has revised axes, while v3 adds a five-panel expert-configuration figure and multiple new comparison and analysis tables.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the evidence for the framework through broader competitors, knowledge/coding/math evaluation and component-focused ablations, addressing v2's narrow comparisons and limited isolation of clustering and routing effects. Clearer motivation and research positioning, together with withdrawal of the lossless-perplexity claim, improve the argument. Removed extended-fine-tuning comparisons and unexplained reuse of some baseline scores under changed shot labels remain material limitations, but do not outweigh the broader evidential and explanatory gains.
